channel.title: Advocates for Self Government – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Advocates for Self Government – Bias and Credibility (theadvocates.org)

item.title: Building a Just World, Part 5
item.description: What would a world built on consent look like? This essay explores consensual governance, polycentric order, and why the right of exit is essential to real freedom.

item.title: Social Security to Start Running out in 2032
item.description: A new CBO report warns Social Security may be unable to pay full benefits by 2032. Here’s why the system is unsustainable and what reforms could prevent a crisis.

item.title: Locked Out of a Living?
item.description: Nearly 1 in 4 American workers now need government permission to do their jobs. Is occupational licensing protecting consumers, or quietly blocking opportunity?

item.title: Are You Being Shadowbanned? Here's What You Need To Know
item.description: Are your social media posts quietly being suppressed? Learn what shadowbanning is, how platforms limit visibility without telling you, and what you can do if your content is being hidden.

item.title: The Truth About First-Time Homebuyer Age
item.description: Are first-time homebuyers really 40? Flawed data says yes. Better research shows the truth and what it misses about the housing affordability crisis.

item.title: Seneca’s Radical Cure for Anger
item.description: Anger feels powerful, but Seneca shows it weakens us. Learn his practical Stoic method to master anger, reclaim self-control, and live more freely.

item.title: Wild, Free, Ungovernable: Zora Neale Hurston
item.description: What if freedom isn’t granted but claimed? Zora Neale Hurston’s fiercely individualist life, seen through the lens of Taoist wisdom, reveals a powerful path to self-governance, authenticity, and living fully on your own terms.

item.title: From Ice Blocks to Refrigeration Abundance
item.description: From iceboxes to electric fridges, refrigeration became vastly more affordable. See how innovation turned a costly luxury into everyday abundance.

item.title: Why Broken People Can’t Fix the World
item.description: Should broken people try to fix the world? This piece argues real change begins with self-mastery, not projection, and warns against outsourcing personal flaws to society.

item.title: Roads Minarchism and a World Built on Consent
item.description: Can a free world run on consent alone? From “roads minarchism” to property rights, this piece outlines a bold framework for peaceful, voluntary order.
